## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

 We integrated Arbitrum as our primary execution layer (Arbitrum Sepolia with Arbiscan explorer integration) for high-speed, cost-effective AMM routing. We integrate Circle (USDC) as our core protocol settlement bridge asset, and our oracle contract architecture strictly adheres to Chainlink's 8-decimal data feed specification

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/yashbaing/HaydenFlow](https://github.com/yashbaing/HaydenFlow)
Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1BtgjZkdNbOZhwCHDrpREuNTfA90NqATN/edit?usp=sharing&ouid=106438885585121001264&rtpof=true&sd=true
Project Link: https://hayden-flow-web.vercel.app/
Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/Ib_eTW61xBM?si=h3n3cRNSD6pA3_T8](https://youtu.be/Ib_eTW61xBM?si=h3n3cRNSD6pA3_T8)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

The rapid growth of tokenized equities (NVDA, TSLA, SPY) revealed a critical flaw in DeFi: forcing every asset into isolated pools against flat stablecoins like USDC.
While traditional finance trades sector baskets and relative value, DeFi suffers from extreme liquidity fragmentation across hundreds of separate USD silos.
Pairing volatile, trending equities against a flat dollar exposes liquidity providers to devastating impermanent loss whenever stocks rally.
Traders also face high slippage and double transaction fees because rotating between stocks requires costly round-trip swaps through cash.
HaydenFlow solves this by introducing correlation-aware liquidity pools that pair assets that naturally move together (e.g., nNVDA/nSPY), slashing impermanent loss by up to 80%.
Its on-chain Pearson correlation engine dynamically adjusts fee tiers based on asset co-movement to maximize capital efficiency and protect LPs.
A Dijkstra smart router connects the entire equity graph to deep USDC gateways, enabling instant trades from any asset with minimal slippage.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

HaydenFlow is unique as the first AMM engineered around statistical asset co-movement rather than naive, isolated cash pairs.
By pairing correlated tokenized equities against market indices (e.g., nNVDA/nSPY), it compresses price divergence and slashes impermanent loss by up to 80%.
Its on-chain 90-day Pearson correlation engine dynamically adjusts fee tiers, rewarding tightly correlated pairs with lower trading fees.
A Dijkstra multi-hop smart router connects the equity network to USDC gateways, eliminating liquidity fragmentation across hundreds of tokenized stocks.
This enables passive liquidity providers to earn safe, sustainable yields on real-world assets without underperforming holding the asset.
It brings institutional relative-value trading and beta-hedging natively on-chain for the first time without intermediate fiat exits.
Ultimately, HaydenFlow provides the high-efficiency liquidity foundation needed to scale the multi-trillion-dollar tokenized RWA economy.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

Calculating 90-day Pearson log-return correlations accurately across volatile assets required designing efficient numerical algorithms that avoid precision loss.
Developing the Dijkstra multi-hop smart router was complex, as it had to discover optimal swap paths across an interconnected graph of correlated pairs in sub-50 milliseconds.
Handling mismatched token decimal standards (6-decimal USDC, 18-decimal synthetic equities, and 8-decimal oracle feeds) required rigorous fixed-point math in the AMM contracts.
Calibrating dynamic fee curves was challenging to ensure fees scale smoothly during asset divergence to protect LPs without killing trading volume.
Synchronizing real-time order routing, live WebSocket price feeds, and interactive D3.js force-directed network graphs required fine-tuned frontend state management.
Bridging Web3 wallet gating with seamless sandbox simulation required robust fallback state machines across all trade and liquidity workflows.

# Haze

Description: Haze is a Uniswap v4 hook that routes high-impact swaps through a commit/settle flow, executing bounded by one of five price limits drawn by Chainlink VRF only after the trade is committed so an attacker can never know in advance how much room a swap will actually have to sandwich. A portion of the premium charged on these protected trades flows straight back to LPs, so the riskiest swaps pay the most into liquidity.
Tags: LP Fees, MEV
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI10

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

I integrated Chainlink VRF v2.5 as the actual source of randomness the whole security mechanism depends on. HazeHook.sol, never generates its own randomness. Instead, when a high impact swap is committed, it calls out to a dedicated adapter contract, VRFConsumer.sol (which extends VRFConsumerBaseV2Plus), that requests randomness from Chainlink's coordinator via requestRandomWords. Once Chainlink's coordinator calls back fulfillRandomWords, a transaction sent by Chainlink itself, the result is mapped to 1 of 5 possible price boundaries, and that's the boundary the trade settles against. This is genuinely external, verifiable randomness: live subscription's request and fulfillment history is visible independently on Chainlink's own VRF dashboard and on Sepolia Etherscan, so anyone can confirm the fulfillment transactions come from Chainlink's coordinator.

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/Dydex/HazeHook](https://github.com/Dydex/HazeHook)
Slides: https://hazehook-pitch-deck.vercel.app/
Project Link: https://haze-hook-4otm.vercel.app/
Demo Video: [https://www.loom.com/share/35a181a711cb4dba85d0973f8523d7ff](https://www.loom.com/share/35a181a711cb4dba85d0973f8523d7ff)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Researching MEV, I found that most trades actually worth attacking are large, high impact ones, since small trades rarely cover a bot's gas cost. I also noticed sandwich attacks do not need to hide a trade, they just need predictability, and a normal swap's fixed slippage tolerance hands an attacker exactly that.

So HazeHook only protects trades that clear a real impact threshold, routing them through a commit and settle flow where the price boundary is drawn from Chainlink VRF only after the trade is locked in, so there is no fixed number left to size an attack against. The premium charged on these protected trades also flows straight to LPs, since large trades are exactly what hurts them most.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

What makes it unique is what actually gets randomized. Most similar approaches change cost, through dynamic or randomized fees, or hide intent briefly, through commit reveal. HazeHook instead randomizes the trade's real execution boundary itself, using genuine external randomness from Chainlink VRF rather than a cheaper on chain shortcut, so the one number a sandwich bot actually needs stays unknown until settlement.

The impact is twofold. For traders, large swaps become genuinely harder to size an attack against, without needing to hide anything or trust an off chain solver. For LPs, the premium charged on protected trades flows straight into their fee earnings, so the trades that carry the most risk also pay the most back, which is a small but real step toward more sustainable liquidity, not just protection.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

One real challenge was security I did not get right the first time. My initial risk check only looked at the size of a trade someone claimed to be making, with no actual cost attached, so anyone could fake a large amount to trigger a paid Chainlink VRF request for free, repeatedly, which would have drained my subscription. I only found this by going back and auditing my own commit function after it was already working.

Another challenge was tuning, not fixing. The price band and the risk threshold pull against each other: widen the band enough to let trades fully fill, and the randomization stops meaningfully protecting anything. Getting that balance right took real iteration, not a single clean answer.

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Liquidity providers on Uniswap v4 face two compounding problems: impermanent loss silently erodes their capital whenever prices move, and static fee tiers fail to reflect actual market risk
  — charging the same fee during calm markets as during high-volatility crashes. Existing solutions either require LPs to actively manage positions or offer no protection at all, leaving
  passive LPs exposed with no recourse.

  ecosystem, HedgeFlow demonstrates that Uniswap v4 hooks can evolve beyond fee customization into full LP risk management infrastructure — a new primitive that could change how protocols

# Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Problem / Background

Today, DeFi liquidity is fragmented and underutilized: LP capital sits in spot pools while perp traders need separate collateral, and risk management is often delayed or manual.
This creates three core problems we wanted to solve:

- Idle LP capital: Uniswap v4 LP positions are valuable but cannot natively power leveraged perp strategies.
- Capital inefficiency: users must split funds across protocols to LP and trade perps.
- Slow risk response: liquidation and repricing workflows depend on delayed/offchain operators, increasing bad-debt risk during volatility.

Our idea was inspired by turning LP positions into active margin: let LPs keep earning in spot liquidity while using that same position as collateral for perps, with automated cross-chain price-triggered actions to keep the system responsive and safer.

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

Impact

What makes this project unique is that it merges spot LP liquidity and perp margin into one capital layer, then automates risk actions in real time.

- Unique value: Uniswap v4 LP positions become live collateral for perps, so liquidity is no longer passive.
- Higher capital efficiency: users can earn LP yield and run leveraged perp strategies with the same position.
- Safer market operations: multi-chain oracle updates trigger automatic repricing and liquidation workflows, reducing lag and bad-debt risk.
- Ecosystem impact: brings deeper utility to Uniswap v4 liquidity on Unichain and demonstrates a practical pattern for autonomous, cross-chain reactive derivatives infrastructure.

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

Challenges

Building this project was challenging because we had to combine three hard systems at once: LP valuation, perp risk engine, and reactive automation.

- LP-as-collateral modeling: correctly valuing Uniswap v4 LP positions under changing prices and using that value safely in margin checks.
- Risk edge cases: handling partial liquidation, bad debt accounting, and keeping account state consistent after close/liquidate/withdraw flows.
- Price consistency: aligning oracle price and vAMM price behavior to avoid inverted pricing or unstable repricing loops.
- Automation reliability: making Reactive-triggered callbacks robust under gas limits and failure scenarios, while ensuring manual fallback still works.
- Testing complexity: building production-like scenario tests (LP profit, LP liquidation, repeated repricing) with realistic parameters and readable diagnostics.

# Helix

Description: Helix is a Uniswap v4 hook that mutualizes impermanent loss across a basket of correlation-diversified LP positions — matching providers whose IL exposure offsets each other and redistributing surplus at settlement so each member converges toward the basket's average IL instead of absorbing their own in full. It uses Reactive Smart Contracts to autonomously monitor cross-chain price correlation and volatility, triggering re-matching or pausing when a basket's risk assumptions break down.
Tags: CCIP, Compliance, DEX, Governance, Regulation
Integrations: Reactive Network
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI8
Date: June 10, 2026

### **Key Links**

- **GitHub:** [https://github.com/aliveevie/helix](https://github.com/aliveevie/helix)
- **Deck / Slides:** [https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1AvHxpYNBWVMhcwZFYfUDPkCNrTQmEeZu82cDTT6Q4eY/edit?usp=sharing](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1AvHxpYNBWVMhcwZFYfUDPkCNrTQmEeZu82cDTT6Q4eY/edit?usp=sharing)
- **Demo Video:** [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9TxX2zQ2xMo](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=9TxX2zQ2xMo)
- **Live Project:** [https://helix-ui-five.vercel.app](https://helix-ui-five.vercel.app/)

### **Partner Integrations**

Uniswap v4 (core): HelixHook extends BaseHook and registers afterInitialize | afterAddLiquidity | afterSwap | beforeRemoveLiquidity, reading real pool price from PoolManager via StateLibrary.getSlot0. ForkLifecycle.t.sol forks Sepolia and runs the full initialize → add-liquidity → swap → settle path against the canonical v4 PoolManager.

Chainlink: ChainlinkOracle implements IHelixOracle, pulling latestRoundData with a staleness guard. Deployed and live as a feed reader against the Sepolia ETH/USD feed. Caveat: the currently-deployed hook instance has its immutable oracle set to a MockOracle — wiring Chainlink end-to-end is a hook redeploy with the same interface, no code change.

ERC-8004 (Trustless Agents): ReputationAccumulator is a conformant ERC-8004 registry. The hook's credit/penalize paths emit ERC-8004 feedback so protocol actions surface through the standard's read path.

Reactive Network: HelixReactive is a real RSC maintaining a volatility EMA and cross-pool correlation estimate, emitting triggerRebalance(matchId, action) callbacks. Deployed on Reactive Lasna, funded, with both Subscribe events confirmed on-chain. Caveat: the live on-chain callback firing from Lasna into Sepolia needs a real volatility event on a subscribed pool — round-trip is demonstrated in test, not yet as an on-chain transaction.

### **Problem / Background**

Every Uniswap LP carries impermanent loss as a silent tax. Existing solutions are all unsatisfying: hedging IL with perps means leaving the AMM, posting margin on a separate venue, and actively managing a position most LPs aren't equipped to run. Insurance-pool designs socialize losses without addressing the cause and need external capital to stay solvent.

The insight behind Helix: the risk often doesn't have to exist — it just has to meet its counterparty. For almost every LP losing to divergence on one pair, there's another LP on a correlated pair experiencing the inverse pull. Those positions never see each other. Capital that is structurally hedgeable stays unhedged purely because nothing matches it.

### **Impact**

Helix is the first IL solution that requires no perp, no external insurance pool, and no exit from the AMM — it turns the LP losing to divergence and the LP gaining from it into each other's hedge. Matching offsetting positions into a basket and redistributing to the average IL provably cuts the variance of LP returns, with the Reactive layer keeping matches honest as correlations shift — all self-funded, so the protocol never holds directional risk.

### **Challenges**

The hardest part was being honest about what "hedging" actually means. The tempting pitch — match two LPs and IL vanishes — is false: matching two concave LP payoffs doesn't create true delta neutrality. Had to rebuild the claim around something provable — mutualizing IL toward the basket average to cut variance, not magically erase the mean — and prove that conservation holds as a Foundry invariant.

Settlement accounting was the next wall: computing IL fairly requires a clean entry/exit price, but pool spot is manipulable, so _settlePrice cross-checks the oracle against each pool's realized TWAP and reverts on divergence.

# Hindsight

Description: Hindsight is a Uniswap v4 hook that decides the fee after your trade: every swap posts a refundable 25 bps bond, and fifteen seconds later — measured on Unichain's 200ms flashblocks — the pool checks what the price actually did and either refunds it in full or forfeits it to the liquidity providers who wore the harm. Re-priced on 55,822 real Unichain mainnet swaps, benign flow pays the 5.00 bps headline, informed flow pays 12.32, and LPs recover 53.8% of the adverse selection they actually suffered.
Tags: Custom hooks, Donation, Dynamic Fee, LP Fees, LVR, MEV, Reputation, Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI10

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

> **Unichain** — the mechanism is flashblock-native. Settlement windows are measured on Uniswap's official FlashblockNumber contract at 200ms resolution (`0x056466f1a50a6B5e4DCCF106074ee0083D721a42` on Sepolia), not on block numbers, which is what makes a 10s maturity + 5s window practical. The hook is deployed on Unichain Sepolia at `0xDecF9FA10d1dE837D96Fca76fE31302D82641aC4`, and the fork test suite runs the full cycle against the real Unichain PoolManager.
>
> **Reactive Network** — settlement is autonomous. A Reactive Smart Contract on Lasna (`0x324d3DA5f40A9D533fe8FfEa7252D7f4b348cE77`) subscribes to the hook's `SwapRecorded` events plus Cron topics and drives `settle()` through the official callback proxy into `HindsightCallback` (`0xF6Dad7BB03a9cf89f4E3b98912Aea695F6b27227`). Swaps settle roughly 45–60 seconds after execution with no keeper of ours running anywhere.
>
> **Chainlink** — the same bytecode is deployed on Base Sepolia (`0xE07a6bb6657f1381e5665F7741DEc4d4eAC8dAc4`), where there is no flashblock contract at all, so it runs a `block.number × 10` fallback clock driven by a Chainlink Automation upkeep (`0x45109C72ED596bBD3786A4C5F36Ae1f88872b206`). That deployment is the proof the mechanism is not Unichain-only: two chains, two independent settlement paths, one verified bytecode.

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/OoJae/hindsight-hook](https://github.com/OoJae/hindsight-hook)
Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1YYsf39G6MripGXETAapgpFGLIWR9arIPITujRHqo3zs/edit?usp=sharing
Project Link: https://oojae.github.io/hindsight-hook/
Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/TL88bUqZwuA](https://youtu.be/TL88bUqZwuA)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Liquidity providers on volatile pairs lose to informed flow. CEX-DEX arbitrage takes the good side of every quote and LPs wear the difference — loss-versus-rebalancing, measured at $233.8M over nineteen months on mainnet, three quarters of it captured by three searchers.

Every fee mechanism we have prices flow before it can know anything about it. A static fee charges retail and arbitrage the same. A dynamic fee reads volatility, but volatility is not intent, it cannot tell a retail swap from a bot. The newest defenses price the intent to be first through priority-fee taxes, but on a fast rollup searchers stop bidding for priority and spam cheap reverting probes instead, and a reverted probe pays zero.

he one signal that cannot be faked, spoofed, or revert-spammed is what the price actually did after the trade landed. Nothing in production prices on it, because pricing after execution means holding something back, and no hook had done that.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

Measured on seven days of real Unichain mainnet ETH/USDC 55,822 swaps, the tape committed to the repo, every figure reproducible offline with one command and no RPC: benign flow pays exactly the 5.00 bps headline, informed flow pays 12.32, and LPs recover 53.8% of the realized adverse selection they suffered ($2,688 of $5,002).

Against a revenue-matched volatility-scaled dynamic fee, Hindsight separates benign from toxic by 2.46× versus 1.27×, and takes about three times less of its revenue from non-informed addresses (5.6% versus 14.4% flat). Charge measured in the first half of the week predicts which addresses adversely select in the second: Spearman +0.739, permutation p = 0.0005 — small sample, 34 addresses, stated plainly.

Because a reverted transaction never lands, it never posts a bond and never enters the measurement, so revert-spam is structurally irrelevant rather than defended against. Live on two chains with two independent settlement paths, 133 Foundry tests, and deployed bytecode verified byte-for-byte against the source.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest part was our own evidence. Three adversarial audit rounds, and twice the audit killed a headline we had already published.

Our own live demo inverted the pitch, the largest markout was acquitted and smaller ones convicted because θ shared a window with the markout it judged, so a trade could raise the bar it was measured against. On the real tape, 927 swaps had been acquitted by their own companion prints. Moving σ to a window that closes before the swap lands made that exactly zero, asserted as an equality rather than a bound.

Then an "out-of-sample" correlation of 0.441 turned out to be 91% tautology a placebo tape with zero predictability scored higher,so we retracted it, published the corrected per-trade figure of ≈0 as a negative result, and replaced it with a per-address split-half test that actually holds. A "0.0% of revenue from benign flow" headline was a string literal, true by construction; the honest number is 5.6%.

Every finding has an executable repro committed before its fix, and all three retractions ship on the site next to their corrected figures. Fitting the fixes in cost us the EIP-170 limit: the hook sits 27 bytes under it.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

I rewrote the contract subscriber-native, rekeying all state by the canonical PositionManager ERC-721 tokenId, while respecting the hard periphery invariant that notification handlers must never revert. Calibrating the scoring and tier thresholds via simulation, and integrating Aave V3 with a safe partial-fill withdraw path, were also significant

# HomeComing

Description: A Uniswap v4 protocol that identifies eligible benign flow, attempts to capture value from private execution, and returns a share of any realized improvement to the pool's LPs — with plain AMM execution as the unconditional floor.
Tags: CoW, LP Fees, LP Liquidity, Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI7

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/Mrwicks00/Homecoming](https://github.com/Mrwicks00/Homecoming)
Slides: https://gamma.app/docs/HOMECOMING-sg6n04y7nqituna?mode=doc
Project Link: 
Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/HymZzUjAwDU](https://youtu.be/HymZzUjAwDU)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Private orderflow systems — CoW Protocol, Flashbots Protect, intent and RFQ auctions — protect swappers by taking their orders out of the public mempool. They do this beside Uniswap, not inside it: the benign, uninformed flow they capture is exactly the flow LPs want, and the value they recapture goes to swappers, wallets, and fillers — never to the pool's LPs. The public AMM is left facing more adverse residual flow while the good flow, and its value, leaves.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

Homecoming is the first of the brief's 660+ prior submissions to integrate a real private venue and route its recaptured value back to LPs — no faked CoW matching, no fork passed off as the real protocol. Its edge is trust-minimized and precise: it verifies the realized on-chain fill instead of an adapter's claim, prices improvement against an exact single-tick quote built on v4-core's own SwapMath, and falls back to plain AMM as an unconditional floor so opting in is rational for traders and never harmful to LPs. The impact is a new LP revenue primitive — value that today leaks entirely to fillers and wallets becomes an on-chain LP asset, turning private orderflow from a competitive threat to the AMM into an outcome aligned with Uniswap's own interests.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest part was discovering the brief couldn't be built as specified: Flashbots Protect has no fill for a hook to call, CoW's settlement is asynchronous and solver-driven, and CoW has no canonical Unichain deployment. That forced a redesign into two separately-deployed legs, with the CoW flow inverted so a real settlement calls into the pool via a post-hook. Beyond that: building an exact single-tick AMM reference on-chain with v4-core's own SwapMath, isolating the venue attempt so failures cleanly revert to plain AMM without leaking funds, and fixing two security bugs caught mid-build — a tick-boundary case that disabled recapture for fresh pools, and a CoW-leg custody flaw letting any caller name themselves as recipient.

# Hook Bazaar - Marketplace for Uniswap v4 Hooks

Description: connecting hook developers with Hook Bazaar solves a critical two-sided market failure: Uniswap v4 introduced hooks as powerful customization primitives, but no infrastructure exists for developers to publish, monetize, and distribute hooks to protocols that need them. Currently, obtaining a production-ready hook costs $10k-$100k and takes weeks—creating an insurmountable barrier for most teams.  Our platform provides a complete marketplace where developers can register hooks with flexible pricing (flat fee, revenue share, or hybrid), while protocols instantly discover, purchase, and deploy pre-audited hooks in minutes instead of weeks. Using the Diamond pattern (EIP-2535), we enable safe multi-hook composition, allowing pools to combine multiple behaviors without conflicts. Revenue is automatically distributed via 0xSplits v2, ensuring transparent, trust-minimized payments between developers and the protocol treasury.  Hook Bazaar creates a self-sustaining ecosystem with three key innovations: (1) standardized hook specifications for safety and trust, (2) developer reputation profiles to drive quality through competition, and (3) optional Fhenix FHE integration for IP-protected premium algorithms. By dramatically reducing costs and deployment time while enabling new monetization models, we're building the infrastructure layer that will accelerate Uniswap v4 adoption and establish "Hook Developer" as a new professional category in DeFi.  Built on: Solidity, Foundry, Uniswap v4, React, TypeScript, Subsquid, 0xSplits v2, Fhenix FHE

# How did you integrate our partners, if any?

Fhenix CoFHE — IP Protection Layer

Encrypts hook implementations on-chain to prevent bytecode decompilation and IP theft.

Encrypted type wrappers (EPoolKey, ESwapParams, EBalanceDelta)
Plaintext ↔ encrypted boundary at CoFHEHook contract
Authorized verifier access for AVS sampling
CoFHE Integration Spec

EigenLayer AVS — Attestation Layer

Provides cryptoeconomic guarantees for hook specification compliance via staked operators.

- HookAttestationTaskManager: Task creation and response handling
- HookAttestationServiceManager: Operator registration and slashing
- Challenge mechanism with 50% slash for false positives, 30% for false negatives
- Off-chain operator runtime for state sampling and compliance checking

# Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Hook Bazaar solves 9 critical market failures in the Uniswap v4 ecosystem:

- No marketplace for hooks — Supply and demand exist but no mechanism connects them
- High barriers to entry — Custom hooks cost $10k–$100k+ and take weeks/months to develop
- No developer incentives — No monetization model or audience for hook developers
- Lack of standardization — No way to objectively evaluate hook safety or correctness
- No hook composition — Cannot safely combine multiple hooks despite v4 support
- No competition mechanism — Best hooks don't naturally rise to the top
- No IP protection — Public code prevents premium algorithm development
- No reputation system — High adoption risk due to lack of trust signals
- Unsustainable economics — No revenue model to support ecosystem growth
- Result: Despite Uniswap v4's powerful hooks primitive, the ecosystem lacks the  infrastructure to enable widespread adoption and sustainable development

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

ok Bazaar is a decentralized marketplace and infrastructure layer for Uniswap v4 hooks that:

For Developers: Direct monetization (flat/revenue-share/hybrid), professional reputation profiles, IP protection via FHE
For Protocols: Instant deployment (minutes vs weeks), lower costs ($100s vs $10k+), pre-audited hooks, multi-hook composition
For Ecosystem: Self-sustaining economic model, quality through competition, accelerated v4 adoption

We integrated Uniswap v4 (hook lifecycle + dynamic fee behavior) and Reactive Network (Lasna) for event-driven risk processing and callback execution. # Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Uniswap v4 hooks unlock powerful pool customization, but they also create new attack surfaces under adversarial flow (sandwich-like bursts, flash-loan-shaped spikes, abrupt price/tick moves, and unauthorized callback attempts). We built HSaaS to give pool operators deterministic, auditable protection that reacts onchain and enforces mitigation quickly without relying on opaque offchain ML.

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

This project creates a full onchain Origin → Reactive → Destination security loop: hook telemetry, deterministic risk scoring, and authenticated mitigation execution. The uniqueness is verifiable enforcement with strict callback authenticity (proxy + RVM binding), replay-safe nonce handling, and tiered fee/throttle/pause controls, which can materially reduce LP value leakage during abnormal market conditions.

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest parts were cross-chain callback authenticity and proving deterministic behavior end-to-end. We had to enforce strict sender/RVM checks, implement replay/idempotence guards, handle Reactive subscription/indexing timing in live demos, and keep mitigation logic robust under edge cases while maintaining strong test/coverage standards.

Stablecoin pools need adaptive fee behavior during depeg/volatility, RWA pools need permission/session constraints, and long-tail pools need launch-phase protections against sniping and manipulation. We built reusable Uniswap v4 hook templates so these policies are enforced on-chain at swap time with deterministic deployment and audit-friendly behavior.

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

This project turns specialized-market policy into reusable on-chain infrastructure rather than one-off hooks. It combines: (1) a shared framework (types/errors/events/guards), (2) 3 concrete market templates, (3) deterministic deployment with permission-bit-safe hook addresses, and (4) verifiable end-to-end demo proof with tx URLs. The impact is faster, safer, and more consistent launch of policy-aware pools for stablecoin, RWA, and long-tail markets.

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest parts were aligning hook behavior with Uniswap v4 permission-bit constraints, enforcing strict PoolManager-only execution paths, and designing guardrails that are both secure and reusable across templates without overcomplicating gas/state. ## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

The idea for HooKeeper was inspired by the realization that Liquidity Providers (LPs) face three compounding risks that result in a "guaranteed transfer of wealth" from them to arbitrage bots whenever price divergence across chains exceeds 2%
. Currently, the threat of Impermanent Loss (IL) is so significant that some users choose to deposit funds in single-asset vaults rather than liquidity pools to avoid it.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

. HooKeeper "recycles" arbitrage bots profits  (on chains like Terra or Injective) by routing them back to the affected LPs.
. HooKeeper is using NEAR Chain Signatures for the Cross-Chain transactions, which allow the system to sign transactions on other chains via an MPC network with no private key exposure eluding the privacy concerns of knowing individual LP balances. HooKeeper preserves LP privacy by using Merkle roots, ensuring that detailed balance data never leaves the Uniswap V4 environment in plaintext
. Hookeeper keeps capital within the ecosystem rather than allowing it to be drained by external bots.

# Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Uniswap v4's introduction of hooks created a powerful new paradigm for DeFi customization, but simultaneously raised a significant barrier to entry for developers. The idea for HookGPT was inspired by witnessing talented developers struggle with the complexity of implementing custom hooks, despite having innovative ideas for DeFi mechanisms.
Many developers had creative concepts for liquidity management, fee structures, or trading strategies, but lacked the specialized knowledge of Solidity optimization, Uniswap v4's internal architecture, and hook development patterns. This created a bottleneck where innovative ideas couldn't be implemented due to technical complexity.
HookGPT solves these problems by democratizing access to hook development through natural language interaction. By training our AI on a comprehensive dataset from Hook Rank's production-grade implementations across multiple chains, we created a system that can:

- Translate conceptual ideas into functional hook code
- Apply common patterns and optimizations automatically
- Handle cross-chain compatibility considerations
- Generate appropriate testing frameworks alongside implementation
- Provide explanations of the generated code for educational purposes
This bridges the gap between DeFi innovators and implementation, accelerating the ecosystem's growth. The project addresses the fundamental bottleneck in Uniswap v4's expanding ecosystem: the shortage of specialized developers who can implement custom hooks for the growing number of use cases.
HookGPT serves primarily as a productivity tool and educational resource that helps developers bootstrap their hook development process, while leaving final verification and security considerations to human experts.

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

What makes HookGPT unique is its specialized knowledge of Uniswap v4 hook patterns trained on production code from existing deployed hooks and specialised rag, enabling developers to generate complex, gas-optimized hooks through simple prompts. This dramatically accelerates DeFi development, making custom Uniswap v4 hooks accessible to a broader range of developers without requiring specialized knowledge of the protocol's internals.

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

Building HookGPT presented significant challenges in training the AI on a diverse corpus of production Uniswap hook code to ensure the generation of secure, gas-efficient smart contracts. Handling multiple chains and their specific requirements required careful architecture, while implementing the contextual understanding needed to translate natural language intents into functional hooks demanded sophisticated prompt engineering.

# Extension: How might you extend the idea with more funding or time?

With additional resources, HookGPT could be extended to include integrated testing and simulation environments that verify hook behavior before deployment, multi-chain deployment automation, and a fully visual interface for designing, testing, and deploying hooks. Adding continuous learning from new hooks deployed in production would ensure the system stays current with evolving best practices across multiple blockchains. This is already a production-focused project with things written in a clean and production-ready manner. I need support and feedback to make it live, as well as funds to fund LLM calls and hosting.

### **Partner Integrations**

No partner integrations.

### **Problem / Background**

Liquidity providers on Uniswap lose money two ways: pool fees don't react to volatility, and impermanent loss silently erodes their capital — over $1.3B/year is exposed to IL on Uniswap alone. Existing tools treat these as separate, manual problems.

The goal was for LPs to be protected automatically, the moment they add liquidity, without managing anything. That inspired HookMind: an AI that tunes fees in real time, plus an on-chain insurance airbag that enrolls every position by default.

### **Impact**

HookMind is the only Uniswap v4 hook combining AI-driven dynamic fees with on-chain impermanent-loss protection that auto-enrolls every LP position — no forms, no separate transaction. Every AI decision is ECDSA-signed and IPFS-audited, giving LPs a verifiable, tamper-proof trail of why each fee changed.

Live on Unichain Sepolia with 87,778 signed agent transactions and 22,823 on-chain core transactions. Makes sophisticated liquidity protection accessible to retail LPs (Market Airbag, tiered coverage) while scaling to institutional positions up to a $10K safety offset per epoch.

### **Challenges**

The hardest part was making AI decisions trustworthy and verifiable on-chain. Built an ECDSA signature + nonce-replay scheme so the contract only accepts fee updates from authorized agents, and pinned every audit log to IPFS. Also had to fit fee logic within v4's hook lifecycle (beforeSwap dynamic fees, afterAddLiquidity auto-enrollment) while keeping the audit surface small — consolidated from 5 contracts to 2, reaching 90.4% test coverage with invariant fuzzing.

# HookMind

Description: HookMind is a non-custodial Uniswap v4 hook that protects liquidity providers from impermanent loss with an on-chain "Market Airbag" that auto-enrolls at deposit, while an AI agent adjusts fees to live volatility. Every fee decision is ECDSA-signed and pinned to IPFS for a full on-chain audit trail.
Tags: Custom hooks, Dynamic Fee, LP Fees, LVR, Machine Learning, Oracle, Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI9

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/Eras256/HookMind](https://github.com/Eras256/HookMind)
Slides: https://drive.google.com/file/d/19bOT3qV7CoiOsLzsl3AnwDwuu7iFEAlZ/view?usp=sharing
Project Link: https://hookmind.xyz
Demo Video: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nmSm5AnFyw](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=2nmSm5AnFyw)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Liquidity providers on Uniswap lose money in two ways that are rarely solved together: impermanent loss when prices move, and static fees that do not reflect real volatility. Most LPs cannot actively manage their positions, so they slowly lose value and eventually leave. We wanted a way for an LP to get both problems handled in a single deposit, with no extra steps.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

HookMind is the only Uniswap v4 hook we know of that combines AI-managed dynamic fees with on-chain impermanent-loss protection that auto-enrolls the moment liquidity is added. The protection, which we call the Market Airbag, is capped, epoch-prorated, and non-custodial, so the pool cannot be drained by a single event. Every fee decision the agent makes is ECDSA-signed and pinned to IPFS, so the reasoning is auditable on-chain. This sits squarely in the UHI9 theme: it is an IL insurance hook and a fee-smoothing hook in one. Lower perceived risk for LPs means deeper pools and better execution for swappers.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest part was making an off-chain AI agent trustworthy on-chain. We added ECDSA signatures, nonce replay protection, and hard fee guardrails (50 to 1000 bps) so the contract stays safe no matter what the agent proposes. Designing the IL protection so it is solvent and capped, rather than an unbounded promise, took several iterations. We also consolidated our contracts from five down to two to shrink the audit surface, which meant rewriting and re-testing most of the core logic.

# HookMind Protocol

Description: HookMind is an autonomous AI middleware for Uniswap v4 that transforms passive liquidity pools into proactive "neural meshes" through off-chain LLM signals and on-chain parametric execution. It utilizes EIP-1153 transient storage for dynamic fee optimization, an ERC-4626 fee-smoothing vault for predictable yield, and a prorated IL insurance pool to institutionalize risk management on Unichain.
Tags: DEX, Dynamic Fee, LP Fees, LP Liquidity, LVR, Machine Learning, Price Discovery, Security, Unichain, Yield Farming
Integrations: Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI8

# How did you integrate our partners, if any?

We integrated Unichain as our primary decentralized infrastructure, optimizing our Uniswap v4 hooks to leverage Unichain’s 1-second block times and EIP-1153 (Transient Storage). This architecture ensures that complex, AI-driven fee adjustments maintain $O(1)$ swap performance without bloating gas costs or increasing transaction latency on the network.

# What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github:[https://github.com/Eras256/HookMind](https://github.com/Eras256/HookMind)
Slides: [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CsPkKX2nm9ep-_BsMR80uyvzoOPSEVBq?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1CsPkKX2nm9ep-_BsMR80uyvzoOPSEVBq?usp=sharing)
Project Link:[https://hook-mind.vercel.app](https://hook-mind.vercel.app)
Demo Video:[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vplEe647F54](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vplEe647F54)

# Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Current liquidity provision in DeFi is largely static and reactive. LPs suffer from Impermanent Loss (IL) and Loss Versus Rebalancing (LVR) because pool parameters like fees don't adapt to market volatility in real-time. We were inspired by the possibility of using Uniswap v4's modularity to build a "Neural Overhaul" for LPs. We are solving the "Static Liquidity Trap" by introducing a proactive layer that adjusts fees and activates protection mechanisms based on real-time LLM analysis of market conditions, preventing toxic order flow before it hits the pool.

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

HookMind is unique because it is an autonomous economic middleware that decouples heavy AI computation from the on-chain swap path. Unlike other dynamic fee hooks, we use an Asynchronous Keeper Model with ECDSA verified signals, preserving Unichain’s 1-second block performance while delivering institutional-grade intelligence. The impact is a self-healing liquidity ecosystem where LPs receive stable, predictable yields (via our YieldVault) and retail users benefit from deeper, better-managed liquidity.

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The biggest challenge was maintaining $O(1)$ swap latency while integrating off-chain intelligence. We overcame this by implementing EIP-1153 (Transient Storage) and a cached state mapping, allowing the hook to read AI-recommended parameters instantly during beforeSwap. Another hurdle was preventing "AI manipulation" via Flash Loans; we solved this by building a Heuristic Deviation Filter in our agent daemon that aborts updates if single-block price movements exceed 15%, ensuring our neural mesh can't be tricked by artificial price spikes.

# Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Impermanent loss (IL) in concentrated liquidity positions on Uniswap v4 can be significantly amplified compared to v2 positions. This creates higher risk for liquidity providers. The project was inspired by Andre Cronje's protection market model for v2 pools, but adapted specifically for v4's hook system and concentrated liquidity mechanics.

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

This project uniquely implements:

- IL calculation specifically for concentrated liquidity positions
- Utilization-based dynamic premium pricing that adjusts automatically with market demand
- Position-specific tracking that requires no external oracles

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

forming the gas-optimized formula to calculate IL based on [https://medium.com/auditless/impermanent-loss-in-uniswap-v3-6c7161d3b445](https://medium.com/auditless/impermanent-loss-in-uniswap-v3-6c7161d3b445)

# Extension: How might you extend the idea with more funding or time?

1. Supporting multi-token protection pools to increase capital efficiency (currently accepts either of pool's token as reserve token)
2. Implementing partial protection options (e.g., covering only 50% of IL for lower premiums)
3. Adding risk tranches for protection providers with different risk/reward profiles
4. Creating a protocol-owned liquidity mechanism to bootstrap initial protection capacity
5. Developing advanced IL prediction algorithms to optimize premium calculations
6. Introducing variable protection periods with term-structure pricing (here I'm thinking of theta based markets like in options trading)
7. Adding support for exotic liquidity positions beyond standard tick ranges

These extensions would require additional mathematical and economical modelling and smart contract development.

# Hyperbola

Description: When your swap would be filled worse than the market's own price, the hook fills part of it from its capital from arbitragers and pays the recaptured value to the LPs.
Tags: Custom Routers, Custom hooks, Dynamic Fee, Dynamic Tick Adjustment, LP Fees, LP Liquidity, MEV, Pool Native Incentivization, Security, Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI6

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/daiwikmh/Hyperbola](https://github.com/daiwikmh/Hyperbola)
Slides: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1i-zaQox3mSLAXktHep_2K3UohA_AsgcYPEmWUqsdisA/edit?usp=sharing
Project Link: https://hyperbola-hook.vercel.app/
Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/T_CCgJdsmmw](https://youtu.be/T_CCgJdsmmw)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Behind every automated exchange are liquidity providers — people who deposit two tokens into a pool so others can trade. They earn fees. But they also bleed value on every price move: the pool always trades at a slightly stale price, and arbitrage bots pick it off. This is the LP's biggest hidden cost, and it's called loss-versus-rebalancing. Traders lose too when your trade overshoots the fair price, a bot trades right behind you and keeps the gap.

Here's the knock-on effect. That bleed gets worse the more volatile the pair. So volatile pools need fat fees often 1% or more — just to make providing liquidity worthwhile. Fat fees kill trading volume. Low volume means thin liquidity and bad prices. The result: today, LPs can really only compete profitably on a handful of deep, stable, blue-chip pairs. Everything else is a money-loser.

Most attempts to fix the bleed either hide your trade behind a private relay you have to trust, or refund you after you've already been exploited.

We found a research paper from Yale — RediSwap (https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.18434) — that proposed auctioning the arbitrage opportunity to arbitrageurs based on the price they believe is fair, and redistributing the proceeds back to users and LPs. It's elegant, but it needs to reorder transactions, which requires block-builder cooperation. Our question: could a plug-in hook capture most of that value and route it to LPs — on any pool, with nothing to bootstrap?

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

The goal: stop value leaking out of LPs, and make volatile-pair liquidity sustainable at a low fee so LPs can compete on any asset pair, not just the safe blue-chips.

For Hyberbola When a trade is being filled on the wrong side of the market price, the hook fills part of it from its own capital from solvers network at a better price, then auctions off what it acquired and donates the recovered margin on-chain, directly to the pool's LPs. That donation is a new revenue stream that offsets the LVR bleed.

Because that recaptured value now goes to LPs, the swap fee no longer has to carry the whole cost of being an LP. A low fee and live liquidity can finally coexist. That's the unlock it makes thin, volatile, and exotic pairs viable for LPs that lose money on them today.

For traders, the guarantee is simple: your execution is provably never worse than a plain pool fair.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest part was making the trader's guarantee structural instead of hopeful. Anyone can build something that's usually better; proving it's never worse is the real work. That meant pricing the partial fill so it always sits between the pool price and the market belief, only acting when the belief is on the trader's favorable side, and then proving it with an invariant test that throws 128,000 random swaps, sweeps, and deposits at the contract in any order.

Uniswap v4's accounting was also tricky. The hook acts as a counterparty to your swap using v4's "flash accounting," where every token movement has to net to exactly zero by the end of the transaction or it reverts — and the permission that lets a hook do this is also the most dangerous one it can hold. Getting the partial fill to balance safely through that path took real care.

Finally, adapting RediSwap from a full protocol design into a single beforeSwap callback meant dropping the transaction-sequencing half entirely and replacing it with a conditional, bounded intervention a different mechanism with its own incentive math to work through. pretty exhausting but fun.

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Modern DeFi publicly links all swap strategies and wallet clusters. We wanted to protect the user's on-chain interaction graph locally without building databases. IdentiFI solves this by moving payload preparation to the user's browser, preventing leaking strategy and setup information before execution.

# IL Shield

Description: A self-funded, on-chain mutual insurance system embedded in a Uniswap v4 pool, where every swap contributes a configurable premium to a shared reserve that compensates LPs for impermanent loss when they exit; with tiered coverage, a deductible, and graceful reserve degradation.
Tags: LP Fees, LP Liquidity
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI9
Date: June 9, 2026

### **Key Links**

- **GitHub:** [https://github.com/acyutaharidas-gif/ilShield_uhi9](https://github.com/acyutaharidas-gif/ilShield_uhi9)
- **Demo Video:** [https://www.loom.com/share/c1ec5cac1ebd4c1a8656fda4eff87872](https://www.loom.com/share/c1ec5cac1ebd4c1a8656fda4eff87872)

### **Partner Integrations**

No partner integrations.

### **Problem / Background**

As far as can be determined, there is no deployed v4 hook that implements self-funded LP insurance. What makes ILShield different is the self-funding loop: the reserve grows automatically from swap premiums, so LP protection scales with pool usage rather than requiring external capital. If it works in production, it could meaningfully lower the barrier for LPs to provide liquidity in volatile pools.

### **Impact**

Every existing solution — external protocols, IL derivatives, farm subsidies — sits outside the AMM. ILShield's IL calculation handles concentrated positions correctly across all three price regimes (in-range, below-range, and above-range), which most implementations skip. The pro-rata cap means the reserve is distributed fairly regardless of which LP exits first.

### **Challenges**

The math was the hardest part. The IL formula for concentrated liquidity requires a proper derivation — three separate cases depending on where the current price is relative to the position's range, all computed in sqrtPriceX96 units using 512-bit intermediate arithmetic to avoid overflow.

Then there's v4's flash accounting for the afterSwap premium collection — getting the hookDeltaUnspecified sign right took real debugging. The pro-rata cap required careful snapshot timing to ensure accounting is correct when multiple LPs exit sequentially.

# ILAL — Institutional Liqu Access and Execution for Uniswap v4

Description: ILAL is a compliance and execution layer for Uniswap v4 that lets institutions settle opposing orders atomically—netting 82% of flow off-chain—while preserving privacy and signed control. It separates access from settlement: Session verifies eligibility via EAS or ZK, and SOEE sends only the residual imbalance to Uniswap v4.
Tags: KYC, LP Fees, MEV, RWA, Stablecoins, zk-SNARK
Integrations: Chainlink
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI10

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

We integrated Chainlink Data Feeds as a fail-closed circuit breaker for SOEE settlement. Before a batch opens, `ChainlinkStablecoinOracleGuard` validates the USDC/USD and USDT/USD feeds for freshness, positive and complete rounds, USD-peg deviation, and pair divergence; `InstitutionalNettingHook` rejects the entire batch before any asset or nonce movement if a check fails. The integration is covered by unit and Base Sepolia fork tests.

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/rpnny/ILAL](https://github.com/rpnny/ILAL)
Slides: 
Project Link: https://www.ilal.tech/
Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/qJnsIrLH89A?si=t4I67k3T3bKdt78Y](https://youtu.be/qJnsIrLH89A?si=t4I67k3T3bKdt78Y)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Two institutions want to trade opposite directions on Uniswap. Neither knows the other exists. Both hit the AMM separately, move the price against each other, and leak value—while separately repeating the same compliance checks they already passed.

With RWA tokenization growing 589% in 2025 and stablecoin transfer volumes exceeding $12.7T in H1 2025, institutional order flow on Uniswap is surging—yet the execution layer has not kept pace. Institutional DeFi execution has two disconnected problems. Compliance and eligibility checks usually happen outside the final onchain transaction, forcing institutions to repeat verification or expose unnecessary identity data, while opposing institutional orders are still routed independently through public AMMs, creating avoidable price impact and information exposure.

ILAL was inspired by this gap: institutional controls should be enforced inside atomic settlement, and Uniswap should process only the liquidity imbalance that actually remains.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

ILAL brings institutional access control and execution logic directly to the Uniswap v4 Hook boundary. Session enables reusable, privacy-preserving eligibility through EAS or ZK, while SOEE atomically nets opposing signed orders and sends only the residual imbalance to the AMM. In our deployed Base Sepolia demonstration, this reduced gross AMM exposure by 82.35%, showing a path to lower price impact, less information leakage, and more efficient use of existing Uniswap liquidity. By enforcing eligibility inside the execution path rather than treating compliance as a separate offchain step, ILAL demonstrates how institutions could access public AMM liquidity while preserving their required controls.For LPs, this means less toxic flow and more predictable returns. For institutions, it means price impact and information leakage are minimized. For Uniswap, it means RWA and stablecoin pools can scale without sacrificing execution quality

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest challenge was implementing atomic netting within Uniswap v4’s accounting model while guaranteeing that only the residual imbalance reaches the pool and that the Hook and Router retain no inventory. We also had to make settlement deterministic for a fixed signed order set, enforce signatures, nonces, deadlines and user-defined limits, and run policy, credential and Chainlink checks before any asset movement. Finally, separating Session and SOEE into independently verifiable candidates—without overstating their current integration—required careful architecture, testing and deployment evidence.

# ILAwareLimitOrderHook

Description: A Uniswap V4 hook that turns every limit order into a yield-bearing, IL-aware position: the filled output earns vault yield, and impermanent loss is computed on-chain from sqrtPriceX96 (no oracle) and rebated from that yield. Live on Unichain mainnet - orders are ERC-721 NFTs, 53 tests passing.
Tags: Custom hooks, LVR, Order Type, Unichain, Yield Farming
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI9
Prize: Uniswap Prize

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/impetus82/il-aware-limit-order-hook](https://github.com/impetus82/il-aware-limit-order-hook)
Slides: 
Project Link: https://il-aware-hook.vercel.app
Demo Video: [https://youtu.be/eikjiI5kq8I](https://youtu.be/eikjiI5kq8I)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

On-chain limit orders are idle capital: your tokens sit locked in the order earning nothing while they wait to fill - and the moment the order fills, you've effectively sold into a moving market and eaten impermanent loss versus simply holding. I wanted a limit order that does the opposite: it puts the capital to work earning yield while it waits, and uses that yield to compensate the user for the IL they incur on the fill - entirely on-chain, with no trusted oracle.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

It fuses two things that are normally separate - execution (limit orders) and capital efficiency (yield + IL protection) - into one Uniswap V4 hook. Impermanent loss is computed on-chain from the pool's own sqrtPriceX96 via a Taylor approximation (the pool is the oracle), and the rebate is provably bounded at min(yield, IL), so the system is always solvent. Orders are minted as ERC-721 NFTs, making a resting or filled order a composable, tradeable asset. As a default primitive, every limit order on Uniswap could become yield-bearing and IL-aware by default.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest part was computing impermanent loss on-chain without an oracle - deriving it from sqrtPriceX96 with a Taylor approximation that stays gas-cheap and accurate. On top of that: keeping the hook solvent and DoS-resistant with graceful execution that never reverts the whole swap and degrades safely when a vault redeem or slippage check fails; O(1) tick-bucket bookkeeping so order discovery doesn't blow up gas; and using V4 flash accounting for exact settlement with no custom token accounting. Covering the edge cases - lossy vault redeem, partial fills, slippage - to 53 passing tests took real effort.

# ILex Hook

Description: Automated Impermanent Loss Protection + Yield Parking for Uniswap v4 LPs, powered by Reactive Network.
Tags: LP Fees, LP Liquidity, MEV, Unichain
Integrations: Reactive Network
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI9

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

Reactive Network — Powers the entire automation layer. An ILexReactive RSC (Reactive Smart Contract) is deployed on Lasna testnet and subscribes to five event topics from ILexHook (PositionCreated, PriceUpdate, PositionExited, PositionReentered, ManualExit). On every swap the hook emits a PriceUpdate event, the Reactive Network delivers it to the RSC's react() function, which evaluates IL for all tracked LPs and fires cross-chain callbacks (triggerExit() / triggerReentry()) back to the hook via the Callback Proxy. No keepers, no off-chain bots.

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/anumukul/ILex-Protocol-UHI9](https://github.com/anumukul/ILex-Protocol-UHI9)
Slides: https://anumukul.github.io/Pitch-Deck-ILex-Protocol-UHI9/
Project Link: https://i-lex-protocol-hook-p.vercel.app/
Demo Video: [https://www.loom.com/share/4ccfa543642949cbbd1c1f66e26c842b](https://www.loom.com/share/4ccfa543642949cbbd1c1f66e26c842b)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Uniswap v4 LPs providing concentrated liquidity face severe impermanent loss (IL) during volatile price moves. Today there is no on-chain safety net — LPs must manually monitor positions 24/7, react to price swings, and execute exits themselves. Existing automation relies on off-chain bots, keepers, or centralized relayers that are expensive, opaque, and introduce trust assumptions. The idea came from the observation that Reactive Network's on-chain event-driven execution could replace all of that with a single, verifiable smart contract.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

ILex is the first fully on-chain, bot-free IL protection system for Uniswap v4. A Reactive Smart Contract monitors price movements, evaluates IL for every LP on every swap, and autonomously exits/re-enters positions — all within the same transaction as the swap itself. LPs set their tolerance once and walk away. The impact is a new primitive for DeFi: programmable, trustless LP risk management that scales to any number of LPs with zero marginal overhead. No keepers, no cron jobs, no relayers.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

- Reactive Network's testnet instability — Lasna underwent an Omni fork mid-development; event ingestion broke on the old chain and the faucet was non-functional on the new chain. Cross-chain automation testing had to be simulated locally via reactive-test-lib and Forge fuzz tests.
- CREATE2 address mining — The hook contract requires the afterSwap flag in its address, which meant brute-forcing salt values to find a valid deployment address — adding deployment complexity.
- Two-chain mental model — Debugging requires reasoning about Unichain Sepolia (hook/lending pool), Reactive Lasna (RSC), and the bridge between them simultaneously. Event delivery failures could originate in either chain or the infrastructure layer, making root-cause analysis non-trivial.

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

Today LPs mostly have two bad options ,stay in the pool and hope the loss disappears, or exit and lock in the loss. # Impact Rebated Fees

Description: A Uniswap v4 hook that charges every swap a refundable deposit, then sixty seconds later uses the pool's own price to decide whether to give it back. Trades that leave the pool still mispriced forfeit the deposit to liquidity providers, and everyone else gets theirs back.
Tags: LP Fees, LVR, MEV, Pool Native Incentivization, Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI10

## How did you integrate our partners, if any?

## What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github: [https://github.com/RaymondAbiola/Impact-Rebated-Fees](https://github.com/RaymondAbiola/Impact-Rebated-Fees)
Slides: https://impact-rebated-fees.vercel.app/deck.html
Project Link: https://impact-rebated-fees.vercel.app/
Demo Video: [https://www.loom.com/share/920d6d2bf94d4078b7269a31e81ba8aa](https://www.loom.com/share/920d6d2bf94d4078b7269a31e81ba8aa)

## Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

A pool quotes one fee to everyone who touches it, but the flow it receives is not uniform. A small fraction of trades is responsible for most of what liquidity providers lose, and the rest of the market covers that cost through a fee kept high enough to absorb it.

What causes the loss is narrower than it first appears. If the price carries on moving in the same direction after a trade has settled, the pool was still quoting a stale number when that trader walked away, and it is about to be picked off again on the same mistake. Eventually the swap fees fail to cover this in most major pools.

Plenty of people have wanted to price that flow separately, including Uniswap, which has an open request for it. Every attempt so far tries to spot it in advance from volatility or a reference price, which is forecasting. That seemed backwards to me. At the moment of the trade there is genuinely nothing to see, because whatever the trader knew has not reached the price yet. A minute later it is obvious. So we let the swap happen, hold a deposit, and look back afterwards.

## Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

The goal is not new. What is new is where the decision sits. Every prior attempt prices a trade before it executes, using a forecast. This one lets the swap settle at the ordinary price and revisits it a minute later, when the answer is no longer a guess. Across the full nine cohort archive of Hook Incubator projects, nothing else settles a fee after the fact.

Getting there took one non obvious choice. The drift has to be measured from the price the swap left behind, not from the price the trader paid. Our first build used the latter and failed outright: across twenty six thousand replayed mainnet swaps it flagged fewer trades than random chance, because a trader's own price impact reverts and pulls everyone toward looking innocent. Moving the starting line removed that bias and the signal appeared.

On a week of real USDC ETH flow the measured effect is roughly a third more revenue for liquidity providers, with an expected cost of 0.71 basis points to a trader carrying no information. That combination is what makes tight fee tiers defensible on pairs currently too volatile to quote cheaply.

It also depends on nothing. No price feed, no keeper network, no off chain service, no partner integration. The pool's own recorded price is the entire input, so any pool can adopt it without inheriting someone else's uptime. The underlying pattern, holding a fee and settling it against what the market later did, is reusable well beyond this hook.

## Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The hardest part was accepting that the first design did not work. I tested it offline against real mainnet swaps before writing any Solidity, and it came back worse than a coin flip. Working out why took longer than building it. The reference point I was measuring from carried a systematic bias, and the fix was separating a trade's own price impact from what the market did afterwards. Had I skipped that offline step, the broken version would have compiled, deployed, and passed every test I would have thought to write.

Deferred settlement is awkward on a chain. Nothing runs on its own, so a verdict sixty seconds later is not something a contract can schedule for itself. That forced a design where anyone can trigger settlement, a bounty makes it worth their while, and an expiry decides what happens when nobody ever bothers. Choosing which way to fail on an abandoned receipt took more thought than the classification did. Computing an average across a window the contract slept through also needed a cumulative counter rather than stored history, so that settlement cost stays flat however busy the pool has been.

Two bugs surfaced only after deploying. Forge routes hook deployment through the CREATE2 factory, so ownership quietly went to that factory rather than to me, leaving the admin functions unreachable. Separately, the hook sees the router as its caller rather than the trader, so refunds were being paid to a contract with no way to forward them. Neither showed up in tests. Both were obvious within a minute of reading live state back off the chain.

The last one was restraint. The parameter sweep contained settings with far better headline revenue, and I did not take them, because they charged ordinary traders three times as much.

# ImpactHook

Description: A Uniswap v4 hook that turns trading activity into verified impact funding. Five funding channels, three verification paths, and behavior-customizable templates that adapt pool mechanics per project type - from router-competitive LP-skim-only pools to traditional swap fee models.
Tags: Cross-Chain, Custom hooks, Donation, Dynamic Fee, LP Fees, Oracle, RWA, Unichain
Integrations: Reactive Network, Unichain
Submission Type: Hook Incubator (UHI)
Cohort: UHI8

# How did you integrate our partners, if any?

- Uniswap Foundation: Novel v4 hook using afterSwapReturnDelta, afterAddLiquidity/afterRemoveLiquidity return deltas, and afterDonate to create five distinct funding channels for impact projects. Behavior-customizable templates adapt pool mechanics per project type. 156 tests, full deployment scripts, 10-page dApp frontend. (src/ImpactHook.sol)
- Unichain: All core contracts deployed on Unichain Sepolia. Integrated Unichain's native EAS (Ethereum Attestation Service) for milestone verification via onchain attestations, including expiration checking. (src/ImpactHook.sol verifyMilestoneEAS function)
- Reactive Network: Cross-chain milestone verification flow. MilestoneOracle emits events on Ethereum Sepolia, MilestoneReactor RSC (inheriting AbstractReactive from reactive-lib) subscribes and relays callbacks to ImpactHook.verifyMilestoneReactive() on Unichain Sepolia via the Callback Proxy. (src/MilestoneOracle.sol, src/MilestoneReactor.sol, src/ImpactHook.sol)
- Arkhai (Alkahest): MilestoneArbiter implements Alkahest's IArbiter interface, gating escrow release on the same onchain milestone state used by the hook. All five funding channels share one source of truth. (src/MilestoneArbiter.sol)

# What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Github:[https://github.com/erinmagennis/ImpactHook](https://github.com/erinmagennis/ImpactHook)
Slides: 
Project Link:[https://impacthook.vercel.app/](https://impacthook.vercel.app/)
Demo Video:[https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1k9cqIy0MnpmuqgcYjrx-cW0ZQmrPWdIq?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1k9cqIy0MnpmuqgcYjrx-cW0ZQmrPWdIq?usp=sharing)

# Problem / Background: What inspired the idea? What problems are you solving?

I've spent the past 5 years working in DeSci and the broader web3 public goods space. The same problem keeps coming up: $2.5 trillion trades daily in crypto, but none of it flows to social impact. Traditional impact funding has three problems: it's slow (annual grant cycles), opaque (donors can't verify outcomes), and unaccountable (money moves before results are proven).

There's no hook in v4 that solves this. Fee-charging hooks exist, but they all make pools less competitive for routing - aggregators skip them for cheaper alternatives.

ImpactHook solves this with the LP fee skim model: a configurable percentage of LP earnings funds the project, while swap pricing stays identical to regular pools. Routers have no reason to skip the pool. LPs opt in. Swappers don't pay extra. This makes impact funding viable even in a fully agentic routing world.

Five funding channels total (swap fees, LP skim, native v4 donate skim, direct donations, institutional escrow), all gated by the same onchain milestones. Projects must prove they're still alive (heartbeat expiration) and hit milestones before any funding releases. Dead projects auto-expire so funders don't have to manage keeping up with them and can automatically and easily keep supporting projects. 

# Impact: What makes this project unique? What impact will this make?

ImpactHook introduces a new class of liquidity pool differentiated by real-world outcomes. Several things make it unique:

1. Router-competitive funding: The LP fee skim model keeps swap pricing identical to regular pools. Most fee-charging hooks make pools less competitive for routing - ImpactHook solves this by funding projects from LP yield instead of (or in addition to) swapper output.
2. Five funding channels, one source of truth: Swap fees (afterSwapReturnDelta), LP fee skim (afterAddLiquidity/afterRemoveLiquidity return deltas), native v4 donate skim (afterDonate), direct donations, and Alkahest institutional escrow. All gated by the same milestone state, heartbeat, and pause controls.
3. Self-enforcing accountability: Heartbeat expiration auto-stops dead projects. Per-project pause lets the owner stop a compromised project without affecting others. Sequential milestone verification ensures progress is proven in order. Three independent verification paths (direct, Reactive Network cross-chain, EAS attestations).
4. Loyalty and retention: Impact tracking per address with configurable loyalty discount tiers. Repeat contributors earn reduced swap fees, addressing the vampire/fork risk inherent in hook fees.
5. Platform, not a one-off: Behavior-customizable templates (lpSkimBps, donateSkimBps, heartbeatInterval, swapFeeEnabled), on-chain registry with metadata, and role-based frontend make this a reusable framework. An "Emergency Relief" template creates LP-skim-only pools (maximally router-competitive), while a "Climate" template enables swap fees with longer heartbeats.

In practice: a clean water project in Chiapas, Mexico could be continuously funded by swap volume on Unichain, with every milestone verified by EAS attestations before a single dollar is released. No grant committees, no intermediaries, no opacity.

Project registration is currently owner-gated for safety, with permissionless registration on the roadmap - progressive decentralization.

# Challenges: What was challenging about building this project?

The afterSwapReturnDelta pattern was the first challenge. The v4 delta system's sign conventions (positive = hook takes from output, negative = hook gives) and understanding how poolManager.take() interacts with the return delta required careful study of core library code and extensive testing.

Implementing LP fee skim via afterAddLiquidity/afterRemoveLiquidity return deltas was the second challenge. The feesAccrued parameter gives exact LP fee data, but getting the checks-effects-interactions pattern right across two currencies with separate POOL_MANAGER.take() calls required careful ordering (flagged and fixed during Slither analysis).

Cross-chain integration with Reactive Network required learning the RSC programming model - contracts run in a ReactVM, subscribe to events on origin chains, and emit Callback events. Getting the authorization model right (checking msg.sender == callbackProxy and the RVM ID matching the project verifier) took iteration.

Hook address mining with CREATE2 was non-trivial - v4 encodes seven permission flags in the address itself. Each time we added new hook permissions (afterAddLiquidity, afterRemoveLiquidity, afterDonate), a new salt had to be mined.

Testing 156 scenarios across 4 contracts simulating cross-chain flows, loyalty discounts, heartbeat expiration, LP fee skimming, and native v4 donate interception in a single Foundry environment was also a significant engineering effort.

# What are the key links to share? (Ex. demo video, GitHub, deck)

Demo Video:
[https://youtu.be/sANXELhElRc](https://youtu.be/sANXELhElRc)

Slides:
